doc.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: His Italian family and the name Jolly
summary: Rowe asks about the surname Seregioli, which became Jolly, and Jolly describes his father's immigration from Italy.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And before we move to Phoenix—
I have to ask you something about your name.
In one of the books I looked at, they had your last name as “Seregioli”

Seregioli. And the gioli became the Jolly. G-I-O-L-I. And it was sort of a nickname that they threw at me and then we decided to use it, because everybody I would say — “Seregioli” well how to do you spell that? Is it a C is it an S?
And then you’ve got to deal with the “ja” is it —
Yeah. There are some names like that. Joe Garigola. It’s similar. It’s Seregioli. My father was Italian of course.
Was he a first generation or had you been in that area for a long time?

Yeah, he was first. Well as a matter of fact I think my grandfather came over first. And dad came over maybe when he was four or five to New York, and then later he became a citizen, because he wasn’t born here. But his sister, my aunt, was born here. So then they moved from New York up to Connecticut. So that’s how the name—
